background: Banco Santander is Spain's largest bank and one of the largest in the eurozone, run as a group of self-funded national subsidiaries across Spain, the UK, Brazil, Mexico, the US and elsewhere, with retail and commercial banking at its core.
synthesis: Ratings are strong at A+ from Fitch and S&P and A1 from Moody's, all stable, with Fitch's upgrade to A+ on 12 May 2026 the latest move. Capital is the weak point against EU and Nordic peers: CET1 of 14.0% is in the bottom quarter and leverage of 4.8% below the peer median, though CET1 has risen 1.0 points since 30 Jun 2025. Liquidity is mixed, with LCR of 147% just below the peer median and NSFR of 124% at it. The one flagged item, on 18 Sep 2026, is strong results at the Chilean subsidiary; the ratings credit a diversification that offsets thinner capital than most peers hold.
